checkedCadence: Weekly source check; urgent changes can be added through the Signal Intel Desk daily task.
method: Sourced, dated estimates only. No fake live counters. Red counters show figures or estimate markers only; titles and explanations render underneath. Where a reliable single estimate is not available, the counter uses an estimate-status value such as EST. SOURCE-SPLIT, MIN. REPORTED, EST. UNDERCOUNT, or STATUS-SPLIT. Crime, sexual assault, trafficking, migrant-status, nationality, ethnicity, suspect, charge, conviction, victim, and report categories must not be merged. This file was checked on 2026-07-06 against official or high-reliability lanes; unchanged live figures mean no stronger sourced replacement was found during the check.

panels.title: Gaza / Israel War
panels.status: Gaza Health Ministry reported death-toll lane; combatant/civilian split contested
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. AP reporting on 2026-06-29 still placed the Gaza Health Ministry death toll above 73,000 since 2023-10-07 and noted continued strike deaths after the ceasefire period. The ministry count does not separate combatants from civilians, and Israel-linked combatant claims must remain separate from reported total deaths. Keep Gaza deaths, Israeli deaths, hostages, injuries, child deaths, famine indicators, disputed official claims, and ceasefire-period casualties separate.
panels.sourceLabel: AP citing Gaza Health Ministry / OCHA OPT / OHCHR / UN Commission

panels.title: Ukraine War
panels.status: OHCHR verified civilian baseline; real toll likely higher
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. The verified civilian-death lane remains above 15,000, with OHCHR warning that real totals are higher. Reuters reported that a 2026-07-01 Russian missile-and-drone attack on Kyiv killed at least 30 people and injured at least 91, while AP reported 2026-06-29 strikes killed at least 12 civilians and wounded 40. Keep verified civilian deaths, injuries, military casualties, missing persons, displacement, occupied-territory reporting limits, and infrastructure attacks separate.
panels.sourceLabel: OHCHR Ukraine / Reuters / AP / UNHCR / OCHA

panels.title: Sudan / Darfur
panels.status: Minimum reported death lane; wider death estimates, displacement, famine, and health collapse separate
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. AP/UNICEF reporting on 2026-07-06 cited at least 59,000 deaths, around 13 million displaced, and more than 30 million people needing aid. Reuters reported on 2026-07-03 that OHCHR warned of siege-like conditions and newly displaced people around al-Obeid, and Reuters/IPC reporting in May 2026 put acute hunger at about 19.5 million people, with 135,000 in catastrophic hunger conditions. Keep verified killings, mass-casualty reports, higher disputed estimates, displacement, famine, hospital attacks, siege conditions, cholera, deportations, and humanitarian access collapse separate.
panels.sourceLabel: UNICEF / OHCHR / OCHA / IPC / IOM / WFP / WHO / AP / Reuters

panels.status: High-uncertainty conflict estimate; source-check retained

panels.title: Global Displacement
panels.status: UNHCR Global Trends baseline for end-2024 / 2025 release
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. UNHCR's latest Global Trends lane remains more than 122 million forcibly displaced people worldwide at end-2024, including refugees, internally displaced people, asylum seekers and others needing international protection. Sudan remains the largest displacement crisis in recent high-reliability summaries. Keep refugees, IDPs, asylum seekers, stateless people, returns, temporary protection, and newly displaced people separate.
panels.sourceLabel: UNHCR Global Trends / AP summary

panels.title: Famine / Acute Food Insecurity
panels.status: GRFC 2025 high acute food insecurity baseline
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. The Global Report on Food Crises lane remains 295.3 million people facing high acute food insecurity across 53 analysed countries. Sudan remains the world's worst hunger emergency in IPC/Reuters reporting, with about 19.5 million people in acute hunger in May 2026; Gaza famine and catastrophic-food-insecurity lanes must be handled separately from the global GRFC baseline. IPC phases, famine declarations, famine risk, siege conditions, nutrition collapse, funding cuts, and humanitarian access restrictions must be tracked separately.
panels.sourceLabel: Global Report on Food Crises / IPC / FAO / WFP / Reuters / Guardian summary

panels.title: Migration / Irregular Immigration
panels.status: Country and route data only; no honest global illegal-immigration counter
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. No reliable single global irregular-migration counter exists. Continue using route/country panels: EU irregular border detections were just over 239,000 in 2024; EU first-time asylum applications were about 912,000 in 2024; U.S. unauthorized-population estimates remain survey/model based; UK small-boat detections passed 200,000 cumulatively since 2018 by May 2026; and Spain received more than 1 million regularisation applications by June 2026 under its status programme. Keep detections, persons, repeat crossings, asylum applications, regularisation applications, returns, removals, departures, estimated unauthorized populations, and missing migrants separate.
panels.sourceLabel: Frontex / Eurostat / CBP / UK Home Office / Pew / AP / Reuters / Guardian

panels.title: Migration Deaths / Missing Migrants
panels.status: IOM 2025 global deaths/missing lane; undercount warning
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. Reuters reported IOM's 2025 global total as nearly 8,000 migrants dead or missing, down from 2024 but likely undercounted due to reduced monitoring. Route examples included Mediterranean, Atlantic/Canary, Asian and Horn of Africa routes. Keep global totals, route totals, confirmed deaths, missing persons, and unverified/undocumented cases separate.
panels.sourceLabel: IOM Missing Migrants / Reuters

panels.title: UK Child Sexual Abuse & Exploitation
panels.status: 2024 police-recorded CSAE lane retained
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. No newer official national replacement was found in this weekly check. England/Wales police recorded 122,768 child sexual abuse and exploitation offences in 2024, with online CSAE reported up 26%. Track offence reports, contact offences, online offences, group-based offences, grooming-gang subset, suspects, charges, convictions, victim age, and data completeness separately.
panels.sourceLabel: NPCC / official police-data reporting / UK media summaries

panels.title: Group-Based CSE / Grooming-Gang Data
panels.status: 2024 group-based CSE lane retained with data-gap warning
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. The 2024 lane remains: 4,450 group-based child sexual exploitation offences across 44 police forces, with 761 linked to grooming gangs. Ethnicity data was recorded in only about one-third of cases, so the site must show both the numbers and the data gap. Keep suspects, convictions, victims, force coverage, and unknown-status categories separate.
panels.sourceLabel: NPCC-reported data / Casey audit lane / AP / UK media

panels.title: Sexual Assault / Migrant-Status Evidence Boundary
panels.status: Country-by-country crime-data lane; no merged group-guilt counter
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. Use this only where official statistics identify suspect nationality, immigration status, asylum status, foreign-born status, or ethnicity. Separate police reports, suspects, charges, convictions, victims, unknown status, and per-capita rates. Do not treat nationality as immigration status, and do not treat individual cases as group guilt.
panels.sourceLabel: National crime offices / courts / police datasets / Eurostat where applicable

panels.title: Trafficking / Sexual Exploitation
panels.status: UNODC 2024 detected-victims lane; child-share included
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. Reuters' summary of UNODC's 2024 Global Report reported 69,627 detected trafficking victims in 2022 and children at 38% of detected victims, with adult women 39%, men 23%, girls 22%, and boys 16%. Sexual exploitation remains a major category for women and girls, while forced labour and cyberfraud exploitation require separate tracking. Keep detected victims, estimated victims, exploitation type, forced labour, sexual exploitation, child share, convictions, and profit estimates separate.
panels.sourceLabel: UNODC Global Report 2024 / Reuters / ILO forced-labour profits

panels.title: Vaccines: Damages & Compensation
panels.status: Compensation and application lane; not raw adverse-event lane
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. The U.S. VICP historical compensation baseline remains above $4.6B where a cleaner HRSA replacement total was not found in this run. UK Covid Inquiry reporting cited 17,519 COVID-vaccine-related VDPS applications and recommended reform of the payment level from £120,000 to more than £200,000. Reuters also reported a 2026 petition seeking to broaden the U.S. Vaccine Injury Table; that petition is a disputed policy/legal claim, not a compensated-injury count. Adverse-event reports, compensated claims, pending claims, rejected claims, causal findings, litigation claims, scheme applications, and disputed table-expansion claims must be separated.
panels.sourceLabel: HRSA VICP / CICP / UK Covid Inquiry / UK VDPS / FT / Reuters

panels.title: Children / Trafficking / Missing
panels.status: NCMEC 2024 CyberTipline baseline; reports not victims
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. NCMEC CyberTipline data for 2024 showed 20.5 million reports of suspected child sexual exploitation, representing 29.2 million incidents and nearly 63 million files. Guardian reporting in February 2026 noted Meta alone made 13.8 million of the 2024 reports and warned investigators are being overloaded by low-quality tips. This is reporting volume, not a count of unique victims or missing children. Missing-child cases, online exploitation reports, trafficking indicators, and resolved cases must not be merged.
panels.sourceLabel: NCMEC CyberTipline Data / ICMEC / UNODC / Europol / Interpol / Guardian

panels.title: Missing Children Cases Supported
panels.status: NCMEC support-case baseline retained
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. NCMEC-supported missing-child cases remain a support-case figure, not total missing children worldwide, trafficking victims, or CyberTipline volume. Keep family abduction, endangered runaway, lost/injured/missing, non-family abduction, recovery, and case-support categories separate.
panels.sourceLabel: NCMEC impact data

panels.title: Online Enticement / Sextortion Reports
panels.status: NCMEC 2024 online solicitation/enticement reporting lane
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. Guardian reporting on NCMEC data cited 546,000 reports from tech firms in 2024 involving adults soliciting children, up 192% from 2023, while NCMEC-related reporting also notes AI-related reports increased sharply. Treat this as suspected-report volume, not proven offender or victim count. Keep online enticement, financial sextortion, AI-generated reports, platform-reporting changes, and law-enforcement outcomes separate.
panels.sourceLabel: NCMEC / FBI / NCA / Guardian / Axios / Wired

panels.title: Medical / System Failure
panels.status: Healthcare pressure lane; theater-by-theater only
panels.description: Checked 2026-07-06. No single honest global medical-collapse counter exists. Use country/theater panels: Sudan reporting now includes more than 30 million people needing aid, siege-like water shortages around al-Obeid, and severe health-system pressure; Gaza, Ukraine, Yemen, DRC, and Myanmar require separate lanes for hospital attacks, medicine shortages, blocked aid, disease outbreaks, healthcare-worker deaths, excess mortality, and service collapse.
